title: SEC0: TLS13 AES-GCM test is round-trip only, not KAT
description: test_tls13_integration step d (crypto2dev_test.c ~line 598-649) encrypts a plaintext and decrypts it, then checks decrypt(encrypt(pt)) == pt. This is a round-trip oracle. It would pass even if the hardware used a completely wrong algorithm (e.g., XOR with a constant) as long as encrypt and decrypt are inverses. The test comment explicitly says 'round-trip verify' and does not provide a fixed expected ciphertext. The test does not detect a bug where encrypt produces wrong ciphertext but decrypt inverts it correctly (e.g., wrong IV applied symmetrically). The existing test_aesgcm_empty() does use a proper NIST KAT with a fixed expected tag; the TLS integration test should also verify a fixed expected ciphertext/tag against a NIST SP 800-38D vector rather than relying on round-trip. wolfssl-bvs.15 notes all vectors come from external sources but does not flag this specific gap in test_tls13_integration.
